svg.text: Each joint: a standard pair of views, plus one extra for a specific question
• Hip: AP · cross-table lateral, + AP pelvis to compare the two sides
• Knee: AP · lateral, + tunnel, skyline or standing when the differential needs it
• Ankle: AP · lateral, + mortise to open up the tibiofibular syndesmosis
• Osteoarthritis looks the same at every joint · a fracture is named by where it sits
STANDARD VIEWS: AP hip · AP pelvis · cross-table lateral
• Ordered alongside a hip X-ray to check for
• Femoral head in the acetabulum · neck · greater and
Hip fracture: named by where the proximal femur breaks
• Femoral neck · greater trochanter · intertrochanteric · subtrochanteric
• Added only when the differential needs
• The tibia and fibula overlap at the syndesmosis
• Opens up the tibiofibular syndesmosis, a full view
FINDINGS: LATERAL MALLEOLUS, graded by Weber type
Weber: the fibular break against the syndesmosis
• A: below · usually stable if the medial malleolus is intact · boot + crutches 6
• B: at · variable, depends on the medial malleolus and deltoid ligament ·
• C: above · unstable, often with a bimalleolar fracture or deltoid injury ·
• Maisonneuve (high fibula) counts as Weber C
Medial malleolus: chip · transverse · vertical · comminuted
• Chip = an avulsion: the deltoid ligament pulls off a flake of
• Comminuted = several pieces, usually high-energy trauma
• Both malleoli + the back of the distal tibia
• No stable bony link between leg and foot: the ankle
• Joint space narrowing and osteophytes, including one on
• The same four signs at the knee
